title: Visa & Consular Services — Embassy of Portugal in Serbia

visa_eligibility.serbian_citizens: Serbian citizens holding a biometric passport do NOT require a visa for short-stay tourism visits up to 90 days within any 180-day period in Portugal/Schengen area. Recommended supporting documents even without a visa: health/travel insurance covering Schengen, return ticket, hotel reservation or invitation letter (especially for stays of 30–90 days). Exception: Serbian passports issued by the Coordination Board (coordinating body for Serbian citizens in Kosovo) DO require a visa regardless of biometric status. Diplomatic passport holders are fully exempt. For stays exceeding 90 days (study, work, volunteering, etc.) a national long-stay visa is required.
visa_eligibility.other_nationals: Third-country nationals legally residing in Serbia who are not Serbian citizens must check their own nationality's visa requirements. Residents of Montenegro and North Macedonia with biometric passports are also visa-exempt for short stays, as the Belgrade embassy also covers those countries.

processing_times.notes: Standard decision period is 15 calendar days from the date the application is deemed admissible. May be extended up to 45 calendar days when further scrutiny is required. An additional 7-day extension is possible when other Schengen member states are consulted (Art. 22 Visa Code). Applications may be submitted up to 6 months before travel (9 months for seafarers). The absolute latest is 15 calendar days before the intended trip. For national (D-type) visas the embassy indicates approximately 3 months processing time. All Schengen applications are currently accepted by email only on designated opening dates — as of May 2026, the next opening is June 16, 2026 (20 vacancies, 9:00 AM Belgrade time). Do not book travel before receiving visa confirmation.

application_location.center: Embassy of Portugal in Belgrade — Consular Section
application_location.booking: All applications are submitted exclusively by email to visas.belgrado@mne.pt on the announced opening date. The embassy publishes vacancy dates on its website and news section. No phone inquiries are accepted for visa matters. Once the embassy responds with a document list, the applicant must submit all documents within 30 days or the process is closed. Appointments for document submission require prior scheduling via sconsular.belgrado@mne.pt or +381 11 2662 895 (Mon–Fri 10:00–12:30). Appointments are conducted in Serbian, English, or Portuguese; applicants without sufficient fluency must bring an interpreter or the appointment will not proceed.

visa_fees.service_fee: External service providers may charge an additional fee not exceeding half the visa fee (~17.50 EUR for Serbian applicants). In countries without a Portuguese consulate, up to ~80 EUR; in exceptional circumstances up to 120 EUR.
fee_exemptions: Students and educators participating in study/training programs
Representatives of non-profit organizations under 25 years attending seminars/conferences/events
Family members of EU, EEA, Swiss, and UK nationals
Administrative appeal fee: 75 EUR (excluding family reunification)

required_documents_all_applicants: Completed and signed Schengen visa application form
Valid travel document (passport) — must remain valid at least 3 months beyond the intended date of departure from the Schengen area
Photocopy of all pages of current passport and photocopies of previously issued passports/visas
Certificate of regular status / proof of legal residence if applying from a country other than country of nationality
Confirmed return travel reservation (flight or other transport)
Travel/health medical insurance covering the entire Schengen area and the full duration of stay (minimum coverage 30,000 EUR)
additional_documents_by_nationality: Serbian citizens with Coordination Board passports: must apply for a visa even though other Serbian biometric passport holders are exempt — same document list as above applies

required: Travel authorization signed by both parents/legal guardians, OR
Court decision granting travel authorization (where applicable)
documents_for_minors.note: If only one parent accompanies the minor, written consent from the absent parent is required unless a court order already grants sole custody.

tourism: Hotel reservation or other confirmed accommodation for the full stay, OR
Written statement of responsibility (invitation letter) from a host in Portugal/Schengen area confirming they will cover accommodation
business: Official invitation letter from the host company/organization in Portugal specifying: purpose of visit, travel dates, name of contact person, and company details
family_or_private_visit: Invitation letter / statement of responsibility from the host (family member or private individual)
Proof of family relationship (birth certificate, marriage certificate, etc.)
Proof of the host's housing conditions (if requested by consulate)
If host is a non-Portuguese EU/Schengen resident: proof that the host is legally residing in Portugal
medical_treatment: Official document from the medical institution in Portugal confirming the need for treatment and appointment dates
Proof of sufficient financial means to cover all medical expenses
transit: Proof of onward travel / confirmed transit itinerary
Visa or residence permit for the final destination country (if required)
Transit airport visa may be required depending on nationality — confirm with embassy

employees: Employment certificate stating position, salary, length of employment, and confirmation of approved leave
Last 3 months' payslips or bank statements showing salary deposits
entrepreneurs: Last 3 months' bank statements for the business account
Tax returns or financial statements demonstrating income
students: Proof of financial means (parental support letter, scholarship documentation, or bank statements)
retirees: Pension certificate or statement showing pension amount

special_provisions: The Embassy of Portugal in Belgrade also has consular jurisdiction over Montenegro and North Macedonia. Citizens of all three countries with biometric passports are exempt from short-stay Schengen visa requirements. The embassy operates a strictly quota-based, email-only application system for Schengen visas: as of May 2026 the next batch opens June 16, 2026 (20 slots). Long-stay national visas (D1–D4, D7, E6) have separate opening dates; several categories are fully booked or suspended (Work Search visa discontinued; D1/D2/D3 and Digital Nomad/D7 dates pending new announcement). Emergency consular assistance (for Portuguese citizens abroad): +351 217 929 714 / +351 961 706 472.
